happy_path.title: A hard refusal sets blocked_at, and later turns are refused without changing the lock
steps: Route not checked against the router (rule AA): POST /api/stream-text/chat/ — Generate a new chat UUID (v4). POST /api/stream-text/chat/<uuid> with a message that clearly breaks a hard rule (for example profanity aimed at the assistant).
Check the response body contains "toolName":"judgeRejection" and "blocked":true.
Query: select user_id, blocked_at, soft_refusals from streamed_texts where uuid='<uuid>'. Note the blocked_at value.
Send 3 more harmless messages to the same UUID, one after another (e.g. 'how do I follow up with a lead?').
Re-run the query from step 3.
happy_path.expected: Step 2: the rejection is returned with blocked:true. Step 3: user_id is test user A and blocked_at is set (not null). Step 4: every response is a judgeRejection with blocked:true and no coaching reply. Step 5: blocked_at is exactly the value noted in step 3 (coalesce keeps the first timestamp), and soft_refusals is unchanged.

happy_path.title: The third soft refusal locks the chat: soft_refusals goes 1, then 2, then blocked_at is set
steps: On a new chat UUID, send an off-topic message that breaks only a mild rule, e.g. song lyrics unrelated to real estate (the tests use rule 'real-estate-focused' as the soft rule).
Query blocked_at and soft_refusals for the UUID.
Send a second off-topic message (different text). Query again.
Send a third off-topic message (different text). Query again.
Send a harmless real-estate question.
happy_path.expected: Step 1: judgeRejection with blocked:false. Step 2: soft_refusals=1, blocked_at null. Step 3: blocked:false, soft_refusals=2, blocked_at null.
